chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' from Salih ibn Uqbah from Yunus al-Nasbani from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'Should I give the Adhan while I am riding?' He said, 'Yes.' I asked, 'Should I give the Iqamah while I am riding?' He said, 'No.' I asked, 'Should I give the Iqamah while I am walking?' He said, 'Yes, walking towards the prayer.' He then said to me, 'When you give the Iqamah, give it with a leisurely pace, for you are in the prayer.'

I said to him, 'I asked you if I should give the Iqamah while walking, and you told me yes. Does it suffice for me to walk during the prayer?' He said, 'Yes, if you enter from the door of the mosque, say the Takbir while with a just Imam, and then walk towards the prayer, that will suffice for you.'

key_terms.أَجْزَأَكَ: It will suffice for you / be valid for you
key_terms.أُقِيمُ: Iqamah (second call to prayer, immediately preceding prayer)
key_terms.إِمَامٌ عَادِلٌ: A just Imam (one who is qualified and upright)

ai.seo_question: Can a person give the Iqamah while walking or riding during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in ritual posture during the call to prayer, permitting Adhan while riding but restricting Iqamah to a standing or walking state to maintain its declarative gravity. The Imam further instructs on the manner of Iqamah, emphasizing a measured, deliberate pace ('mutarrasilan') to reflect reverence, while validating the transition from walking to prayer as part of the congregational entry, thereby linking physical movement with spiritual presence.
